question: It is given that $X\begin{bmatrix}3&2\\ 1&-1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4&1\\ 2&3\end{bmatrix}$. Then matrix $X$ is:
explanation:
**Step 1: Define relationship.** Let $A = \begin{bmatrix}3&2\\ 1&-1\end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix}4&1\\ 2&3\end{bmatrix}$. The given equation is $XA = B$, which means $X = BA^{-1}$.
**Step 2: Find the inverse of A.** The determinant $|A| = (3)(-1) - (2)(1) = -3 - 2 = -5$. The adjoint of $A$ is $\begin{bmatrix}-1&-2\\ -1&3\end{bmatrix}$. Thus, $A^{-1} = -\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}-1&-2\\ -1&3\end{bmatrix}$.
**Step 3: Multiply matrices.** Compute $X = \begin{bmatrix}4&1\\ 2&3\end{bmatrix} \left(-\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}-1&-2\\ -1&3\end{bmatrix}\right)$. This yields $-\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}(4)(-1)+(1)(-1) & (4)(-2)+(1)(3)\\ (2)(-1)+(3)(-1) & (2)(-2)+(3)(3)\end{bmatrix} = -\frac{1}{5}\begin{bmatrix}-5&-5\\ -5&5\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1&1\\ 1&-1\end{bmatrix}$.
